Definition: from G4862 and G4762; to twist together, i.e. collect (a bundle, a crowd):--gather.
BiblicalUsage: Matthew uses the word for Jesus and the disciples gathered together in Galilee, when He tells them again of His death. Luke uses it for Paul gathering a bundle of sticks on Malta, and the viper that came out of the heat. Gathering is the sense in both: people drawn together, or sticks twisted into one bundle.
TheologicalSignificance: The two scenes belong together in a quiet way, I believe: Jesus gathers His own before the cross, and Paul simply gathers sticks, and God is at work in both.
